title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection heuristics and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: Our performance canary pipeline occasionally misses small latency regressions when workload distributions change and has produced noisy false positives during scheduled traffic shifts. This PR improves the auto-detection heuristics and adds conservative rollout guards to prevent automated rollouts from triggering on transient signals. Changes include: 1) multi-window detection: computes regressions across short/medium/long windows and requires corroboration before marking a regression; 2) adaptive baseline selection: uses cluster-aware baselines (region, model-variant, instance-type) when available; 3) hysteresis and cooldown: adds a cooldown period and step-down thresholds before an automated rollback/rollout; 4) synthetic canary weighting: blends synthetic and production canaries to reduce sensitivity to scheduled production spikes; 5) expanded integration tests + canary ingestion validation. The PR includes config defaults tuned conservatively, migration notes for existing canaries, and metrics/dashboards updates. See Linear ENG-7921 and ENG-8013 for context. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by SRE/team - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Load-tested in perf-canary lab - [x] Docs updated (console + runbooks) - [x] Rollout gating for Dedicated clusters

discussion_notes: Key trade-offs: conservative defaults reduce automated recovery speed but avoid false positive rollouts. We opted to require corroboration across at least two detection windows and either synthetic or production canary signal when traffic is low. Migration: existing canaries will pick up new defaults; operator can opt-in to aggressive mode via helm/console. Backwards compatibility: no breaking changes to observer API.
release_notes: Performance canary: improved auto-detection to reduce false positives, added rollout guards (cooldown, hysteresis), adaptive baselines for heterogeneous clusters, and synthetic/production weighting. Operators should review new defaults before enabling aggressive rollouts.
